note: Proposes a benchmark lifecycle covering design, validation, monitoring and retirement, an audit ready framing.
title: Beyond the Leaderboard: A Survey of the Science of Evaluation, Benchmarking, and Methodologies for Large Language Models
explain_beginner: This paper identifies a major problem in AI: popular test scores for large language models do not actually measure what we think they measure. Although these AI systems score well on standard tests, they often fail in real situations by making mistakes or producing harmful content. The researchers argue we need better evaluation methods that assess genuine capabilities rather than pursuing high scores on leaderboards. They propose a structured lifecycle for creating, checking, and retiring evaluation tools to make progress measurement more trustworthy.
explain_business: Organizations deploying large language models face a critical risk: public benchmark scores do not predict real-world performance. This paper demonstrates why relying solely on leaderboard rankings to select models is unreliable and why purchased or built systems may underperform expectations. The proposed Benchmark Lifecycle framework provides a structured methodology for enterprises to properly evaluate AI systems before deployment, reducing failure risk. This guidance helps organizations establish evaluation as a scientific process rather than a competitive metric, ensuring confident decision-making for AI investments.
explain_practitioner: The survey examines the disconnect between benchmark performance and practical LLM capabilities, attributing it to static evaluation paradigms. The authors present a taxonomy covering five evaluation approaches: static benchmarks, dynamic adaptive evaluation, interactive agentic evaluation, human-in-the-loop methods, and model-based evaluation. They analyze key pathologies including data contamination and leaderboard gaming. The central contribution is the Benchmark Lifecycle framework, which systematizes evaluation instrument development through design, validation, deployment monitoring, and retirement phases to enable rigorous measurement aligned with actual model behavior.
